## CHAD — profile (page 142)

- Header facts: Sub-Saharan Africa; Low-income; IDA; Preliminary data (P); Population 21.0 million; GNI 20,500; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock 2025: 3,457, up +3.2% from 2024.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25:
  - Printed start/end values: 2,799 (2015) and 3,457 (2025).
  - Line shape: debt rises from 2015 through the late 2010s, continues upward to a peak around 2022 at ≈3.8 billion, then falls in 2023 and again slightly in 2024, before recovering in 2025 to 3,457.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 3,457
  - Public & publicly guaranteed (PPG): 3,428
  - Short-term: 29
  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:
    - Multilateral: 1,744
    - Bilateral: 1,550
    - Private creditors: 134
  - Multilateral:
    - IMF credit: 614
    - BDEAC: 283
    - Other multilateral: 847
  - Bilateral:
    - United Arab Emirates: 650
    - Libya: 246
    - Other bilateral: 654

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 57%, +7.1%; trend rises early, fluctuates, and ends above its 2015 level.
  - External debt / GNI: 17%, -3.5%; trend is fairly stable with mild fluctuations, edging down by 2025.
  - Debt service / exports: 5%, -18.3%; trend is volatile, peaking around the early 2020s at ≈7%, then declining to 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 1%, -26.4%; trend rises from a low base to a peak around 2023 at ≈2%, then falls back by 2025.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors:
    - Maturity: 23 yrs
    - Grace period: 6 yrs
    - Interest rate: 1.4%
  - Private creditors:
    - Maturity: ..
    - Grace period: ..
    - Interest rate: ..

- Notes/Source:
  - Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
  - Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
